easy.def: People.
examples: Hello, folks!
Kind folks live here.
The folks next door are nice.

more.def: People, especially a group of people or a family.
examples: Welcome, folks, to the show!
The folks next door brought us cookies.
The old folks sat on the porch.

easy.def: To go after someone or something.
examples: The ducklings follow their mom.
My dog follows me everywhere.
Follow me to the door.

more.def: To go or come after someone or something.
examples: The baby ducks follow their mother in a straight line.
A police car followed the ambulance down the road.
Follow the path to the lake.

easy.def: To do what a rule or directions say.
examples: Follow the rules.
We followed the recipe.
Follow the map.

more.def: To do what directions, rules or advice say.
examples: Please follow the directions on the box carefully.
She followed the recipe to bake the cake.
Cars must follow the traffic signs.

easy.def: Things that you eat.
examples: Pizza is my favorite food.
The cat eats cat food.
Birds look for food in the snow.

more.def: What people and animals eat to live and grow.
examples: Farmers grow food for the whole town.
Bears eat a lot of food in the fall before winter.
Plants make their own food using sunlight.

easy.def: A person who does silly things.
examples: I felt like a fool when I fell.
Only a fool would walk on thin ice.
The fool in the story danced on the table.

more.def: A person who acts without thinking or does something silly.
examples: He felt like a fool when he put his shirt on backward.
The clown played the fool to make us laugh.
Only a fool would go out in the storm without a coat.

easy.def: To trick someone.
examples: You can't fool me.
The magician fooled us.
The fake spider fooled my sister.

more.def: To trick someone into believing something that is not true.
examples: The magician fooled the whole audience with his card trick.
The bird's song fooled the cat into looking up.
You cannot fool me because I saw you hide it.

easy.def: The part you stand on, at the end of your leg.
examples: My foot hurts.
Put your left foot in the shoe.
A baby's foot is tiny.

more.def: The part of the body at the end of the leg, which you stand and walk on.
examples: She stubbed her foot on the leg of the table.
A duck's webbed foot helps it paddle through the water.
The soccer player kicked the ball with the side of her foot.

easy.def: A way to measure how long something is.
examples: My bed is six feet long.
The fish was one foot long.
The fence is four feet tall.

more.def: A unit of length equal to 12 inches, used to measure how long or tall something is.
examples: The snowman was about five feet tall.
A baseball diamond is ninety feet from base to base.
The pool is three feet deep at one end.

easy.def: The bottom part of something.
examples: The shop is at the foot of the hill.
Put a blanket at the foot of the bed.
The cabin sits at the foot of the mountain.

more.def: The lowest part of something, such as a hill, a bed or a set of stairs.
examples: A small village lay at the foot of the mountain.
The cat curled up at the foot of my bed.
Wait for me at the foot of the stairs.

easy.def: A word that shows who gets something or why.
examples: This card is for you.
I saved a seat for Dad.
We have a treat for the dog.

more.def: A word used to show who gets something, what its purpose is, or how long something lasts.
examples: The nurse made a bandage for my scraped knee.
We waited for the bus for ten minutes.
A saw is a tool for cutting wood.

easy.def: A push or pull.
examples: Wind has force.
A magnet pulls with force.
The force of the wave knocked me over.

more.def: A push or pull that makes something move or change.
examples: The force of the wind blew the door shut.
Gravity is a force that pulls things toward the ground.
It takes a lot of force to push the heavy cart.

easy.def: To make something happen by using strength.
examples: He forced the stuck door open.
Do not force the puzzle piece.
Mom forced the lid off.

more.def: To make a person or thing do something by using strength or power.
examples: The storm forced us to stay inside.
She forced the stuck window open.
Heavy rain forced the game to stop.

easy.def: A big place with lots of trees.
examples: Deer live in the forest.
An owl hooted in the forest.
We camp in the forest.

more.def: A large area of land covered with trees and other plants.
examples: We followed a narrow trail through the forest.
The forest floor was covered with fallen leaves.
Many animals lost their homes when the forest burned.

easy.def: To not remember.
examples: I forget his name.
She forgot her hat.
Do not forget me.

more.def: To be unable to remember something, or to not do it because you did not think of it.
examples: I forgot where I put my library book.
Do not forget to feed the fish before you go.
He has never forgotten the day he saw a whale.

easy.def: To stop being angry at someone.
examples: I forgive you.
She forgave her friend.
Please forgive me.

more.def: To stop being angry with someone who has done something wrong.
examples: He forgave his sister for breaking the toy.
Please forgive me for being late.
She forgave her friend after the argument.

easy.def: A kind of something.
examples: Ice is a form of water.
Water has three forms.
Steam is a form of water.

more.def: A kind of something, or the shape it takes.
examples: Ice is a solid form of water.
Poetry is one form of writing.
Clouds appear in many forms.

easy.def: A paper with spaces to fill in.
examples: Fill out the form.
The form needs your name.
Sign the form.

more.def: A paper with blank spaces where you write information.
examples: Please fill out the form with your name and age.
The library card form asks for your address.
She signed the form and handed it back.

easy.def: To make or shape something.
examples: Ice forms on the pond.
We formed a line.
Clouds form in the sky.

more.def: To make something, or to come into being.
examples: Ice forms on the pond in winter.
We formed a line at the door.
Clay can be formed into a bowl.

easy.def: Toward the front.
examples: Step forward.
Move forward.
The car rolled forward.

more.def: In the direction that is in front of you.
examples: Please step forward and take a ticket.
The line moved forward.
He leaned forward to hear better.

easy.def: A very old bone or mark from a plant or animal, found in rock.
examples: We saw a dinosaur fossil.
I found a fossil of a shell.
The fossil is in a rock.

more.def: What is left of a plant or animal from long ago, kept safe in rock.
examples: The fossil showed the shape of a fish that lived millions of years ago.
Fossils help scientists learn about animals from long ago.
He found a leaf fossil in a piece of stone.

easy.def: The number 4.
examples: I have four crayons.
Four plus one is five.
A cat has four legs.

more.def: The number 4, which is one more than three.
examples: A year has four seasons.
We saw four deer by the road.
The clock struck four.

easy.def: One more than thirteen.
examples: She has fourteen pencils.
My brother is fourteen.
Fourteen ducks swam by.

more.def: The number 14, which comes after thirteen and before fifteen.
examples: Two weeks is fourteen days.
The bus has fourteen rows of seats.
He read fourteen books this summer.
